correctness.rationale: For positive concurrence a Bell-diagonal state has a unique eigenvalue above one half; relabel it as \(p_1=(1+C)/2\) and write the other three masses as \(q_i\). The absolute correlation coordinates are exactly \(r_i=C+2q_i\), hence \(r_i\ge C\) and \(r_1+r_2+r_3=1+2C\), with the converse reconstruction \(q_i=(r_i-C)/2\). Ordering \(x\ge y\ge z\), Hilbert--Schmidt geometric discord is \((y^2+z^2)/4\) and the feasible slice is the triangle \(z\ge C\), \(y\ge z\), \(2y+z\le1+2C\). Its vertices give the lower value \(C^2/2\), the rank-three face value \((1+2C+5C^2)/16\), and the isotropic value \((1+2C)^2/18\). Convexity places the maximum at a vertex, and the difference factors as \((1-C)(13C-1)/144\), yielding the exact crossover \(C=1/13\). At \(C=0\), direct optimization on the separable octahedron gives lower zero and upper \(1/16\). Connectedness of the fixed-concurrence slice and continuity of discord prove that the full interval between endpoints is attained. The exact-rational verifier independently checks extremal families, crossover, and a large rational grid; the continuum theorem rests on the triangle proof.
residual_risks: The result uses the squared Hilbert--Schmidt geometric discord, whose known resource-monotonicity limitations are not addressed.

Their full text also quotes the sharp Bell-violation interval at fixed concurrence and records the Werner concurrence--discord relation, but it does not optimize Hilbert--Schmidt discord itself over the fixed-concurrence Bell-diagonal slice. A complete fixed-concurrence attainable interval with explicit extremizers and a genuine branch switch at \(1/13\) is a natural exact state-space classification. Its value is structural rather than dependent on the disputed operational status of Hilbert--Schmidt discord.
